Design and apply an FIR filter.

A windowed-sinc FIR filter (scipy.signal.firwin) designed from the settings and applied zero-phase (centred; the rows beyond the ends repeat the edge value) to one numeric column, added as &lt;column>_filtered beside every input column.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Category | [Signal](../categories/signal.md) |
| Status | Runs |
| Also read from graphs as | `FilterDesigner` |
| Search words | filter, fir, firwin, lowpass, highpass, bandpass |

## Inputs

| Pin | Type | Required | Connections | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Data** | Dataset | Yes | 1 | Input table containing the signal column |

## Outputs

| Pin | Type | Required | Connections | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Filtered** | Dataset | Yes | 1 | Input table plus &lt;signal_col>_filtered |

## Settings

| Setting | Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Read by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| signal_col | `signal_col` | Text | (empty) |   | The run | Numeric signal column. Required. |
| filter_type | `filter_type` | Choice | `lowpass` | `lowpass`, `highpass`, `bandpass`, `bandstop` | The run | Filter type. |
| cutoff | `cutoff` | Number | `0.1` | `> 0 and below sample_rate / 2` | The run | The cutoff, per second at the sample rate (below Nyquist) |
| cutoff_high | `cutoff_high` | Number | `0` | `Greater than cutoff for band filters` | The run | Upper cutoff required by bandpass and bandstop. |
| sample_rate | `sample_rate` | Number | `1.0` | `> 0` | The run | Samples per second (per unit, per row) |
| taps | `taps` | Integer | `31` | `>= 3` | The run | Coefficients; odd for highpass and bandstop. |
| window | `window` | Choice | `hamming` | `hamming`, `hann`, `blackman`, `boxcar` | The run | The window of the sinc (symmetric) |

**Read by** says whether a run uses the setting (**The run**) or only the editor, a dialog or a view (**The editor only**).

## Where it runs

| Where | Runs |
